newsitem.title: UK: Celltech doesn't expect CDP 571 to developed.
newsitem.headline: Celltech doesn't expect CDP 571 to developed.

text.p: British biotechnology group Celltech Plc said on Wednesday that as a result of findings by Germany's Bayer AG with BAYX-1351 in septic shock treatment, it did not expect the second generation novel anti-TNF antibody CDP 571 to be developed further.
This was Celltech's first collaborative venture with Bayer, whose septic shock trial results had been imminent.
Celltech said in a statement that it now expected to regain the development rights for CDP 571 in chronic conditions, which would include Crohn's disease.
Bayer has applied for U.S. regulatory approval to enable a Phase II study to be undertaken into Crohn's disease and, subject to approval, Celltech intends to begin this study soon.

Celltech said in the statement that the company remained financially "very strong" and had collaborative agreements with a range of international pharmaceutical companies and four novel product candidates in Phase III clinical development.
It added that it also had a pipeline of novel compounds in pre-clinical development as well as important revenue generating intellectual property.
Celltech's share price more than halved on the news and was last 342-1/2 pence down at 287-1/2 pence.
